trigger: www.xbox.com/sitemap.xml is a sitemap INDEX (930 child <sitemap> entries) pointing to gzip-compressed sitemap chunks (e.g. pdp-en-US-sitemap-0.xml.gz, cms-sitemap-0.xml.gz), not plain XML. The original per-request cap (750,000 bytes, sized for HTML pages) truncated the first chunk (pdp-en-US-sitemap-0.xml.gz) mid-file as raw application/gzip bytes -- AccessProbe.probe() also text-decodes bytes, which corrupts binary gzip content beyond just truncation. Neither problem can be fixed within the original budget's document handling; a bounded, Range-aware, byte-preserving fetch (the same mechanism proven in Stage 8.6 for PDFs) is required.

revision.applies_to: gzip sitemap document fetches only (www.xbox.com/sitemap/*.xml.gz); does NOT change the original 750,000-byte cap used for ordinary HTML page fetches via AccessProbe.probe()
revision.reasoning_for_8mb_cap: Conservative first cap, not yet informed by an observed file size (unlike Stage 8.6's revision, which raised its cap only after seeing the confirmed real total via Content-Range). If a document's own declared Content-Range total exceeds this, the fetch stops immediately (unknown_completeness) and is reported as such, not silently retried with an ever-larger cap.
revision.target_this_stage: https://www.xbox.com/sitemap/cms-sitemap-0.xml.gz first (a single CMS/content-page sitemap chunk, most likely to contain a canonical hardware landing page such as an 'Xbox Series S' page, rather than one PDP-per-SKU-per-market entry among the 930 PDP chunks). PDP chunks are only opened afterward, and only if the CMS chunk does not yield a usable candidate, each requiring its own added per-chunk budget line before being fetched.
